briefdescription.para: _NODE_STATUS row field offsets, in bytes of the decoded row (hex index = 2 × offset).

detaileddescription.para: Each field is its numeric value as fixed-width uppercase hex, most-significant byte first, so the u16 fields read big-endian here although they are little-endian on CAN. A field runs to the next offset; the last runs to NODE_STATUS_ROW_BYTES. The first six come from the node's HB_n (plus present), the last five from its HEALTH_n. (Not NODE_ID: every node build defines that as a macro.)

briefdescription.para: _NODE_TELEM row field offsets, in bytes of the decoded row (hex index = 2 × offset).
HB_n flags bits — CAN controller error state (maps to HeartbeatPayload.flags).
HEALTH_n flags bits — node-level health conditions (maps to NodeHealthPayload.flags).
HEALTH_n faultId dictionary (#163) — cross-node fault codes.

detaileddescription.para: Coarse, one active at a time on the wire; the exact device is logged locally on DiagSerial, not the frame. The client maps id → human label (SkyHawkClient#40). Each node type contributes the codes relevant to its fault sources; append as new sources appear.

briefdescription.para: HEALTH_n nodeKind (byte 5) — what kind of board this node is (#344).

detaileddescription.para: Announced by the board's own firmware role (each node library passes its kind to CANProtocol::serviceNodeStatus()), never derived from the NODE_ID — a PDU can take any ID. Append-only. 0x00 is what firmware older than #344 sends (the byte was reserved), so the client reads it as "unknown" and never adopts on it.

briefdescription.para: TELEM_n page ids (#216) — byte 0 of TelemPayload, naming the layout of bytes 1-7.

detaileddescription.para: Global and append-only: a page id means the same layout whichever node sends it, so the client decodes by page, not by node type. 0x00 is invalid. Each page's layout is its field-offset enum below (PDU_RAIL_* → PduRailField, PDU_STATUS → PduStatusField); multi-byte fields little-endian.

briefdescription.para: PDU_RAIL_* page byte 1 — per-rail condition bits (all zero = healthy).
PDU_STATUS page byte 1 — board condition bits (all zero = healthy, calibrated).
PDU_RAIL_12V / PDU_RAIL_5V field offsets, in bytes of the 8-byte TELEM_n frame.

detaileddescription.para: Byte 0 is the TelemPage; a field runs to the next offset, the last to byte 7. Little-endian.

briefdescription.para: PDU_STATUS field offsets, in bytes of the 8-byte TELEM_n frame.

detaileddescription.para: Byte 0 is the TelemPage; a field runs to the next offset, the last to byte 7. Little-endian.

briefdescription.para: Node ID of the Gateway board's PanelBridge MCU — the CAN master.

detaileddescription.para: It sends HB_0 / HEALTH_0, and its own row leads every _NODE_STATUS roster reply (#344). CAN nodes take 1–63 (Firmware/NODE_IDS.md).

briefdescription.para: _NODE_STATUS row length in bytes, sent as twice as many hex chars (proto v3: 14 → 28 hex).
_NODE_TELEM row length in bytes, sent as twice as many hex chars (9 → 18 hex).
HB_n esr field: bit position of the transmit error counter (TEC, low byte).
HB_n esr field: bit position of the receive error counter (REC, high byte).
HEALTH_n dieTempC meaning "unavailable / not yet seen" (80 on the wire).

detaileddescription.para: Sent when the die sensor can't be read, and cached by PanelBridge for a node whose first HEALTH_n hasn't arrived. Written as a literal so the client sync can read it; equal to INT8_MIN.

briefdescription.para: PDU_STATUS ntcTempDC meaning "unavailable" — no reading yet, or the NTC is open/shorted.

detaileddescription.para: 0x8000 on the wire. Written as a literal so the client sync can read it; equal to INT16_MIN.

briefdescription.para: Neutral node-status contract for every OpenSkyhawk node (PanelGroup, PanelBridge, PDU).

detaileddescription.para:
Every wire value is a named enum class X : T { NAME = literal } or constexpr T NAME = literal so the client sync can read it (#346) — never only a comment, a bare literal or a format string.
FaultSource — the interface a fault-producing object implements so a node-level aggregator can roll it up. A FaultSource is one piece of node status, not the whole story.

This is the neutral home for node-status vocabulary so it isn't shaped around any one node flavour (PanelGroup/OutputBase) or the HID namespace. NodeHealthPayload (the CAN HEALTH_n frame struct) stays in CANProtocol.h; the fault detail strings stay local (DiagSerial), never on the wire. Header-only contract + a tiny FaultSource registry (NodeStatus.cpp).
